title: Word families (B1)
note: act → action → active → actively. Transformation across the four word classes, and the direct feeder for the RUE3 word-formation mode. Plays after b1_suffixes and b1_prefixes. · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: this pack was unplayable at Quiz and Type. Every item's `en` was the PAIR string (*decide → decision*), so with quiz_mode sentence_gap and eight sentences that contained no such string, sentenceToFrame produced **zero** frames — all 36 words fell back to matching an arrow string against a Czech arrow string, in every stage. · Rebuilt on B7, which this pack's own note already asked for: every item is an FCE cloze — a full sentence, a gap, and the root in CAPITALS — carried on the item as gap/gap_answer, so Match is still word↔word (12 per board, B9) and Quiz/Type are the transformation. · B6: quiz_options are authored on all 36 — the correct form, the ROOT itself, and a wrong derivation of the same root (~~noiseful~~, ~~easyly~~, ~~goodly~~). The fallback would have offered another family's noun, which tests nothing. · The six transformation tables are kept and a seventh card carries the two that break the rule: good→well, and hard→hard with **hardly** named as a different word (*sotva*). E10: Use is use_mode rewrite, 12 items — the prompt carries the base form, the answer needs the derived one, which is the whole job of this unit. · Pool-checked against everything taught before leaf_word_families_b1 — 0 unknown types. · 2026-09-04: all twelve rewrite items — a word-family target changes word class, so the prompt must already stand in the target's class. Every prompt now differs from its answer by exactly the underlined phrase.

intro.title: Two that do not follow the rule
intro.note: **hardly** is not the adverb of *hard*. *He works hard* = usilovně. *He hardly works* = sotva pracuje.
intro.note_cz: Pozor: hardly ≠ hard. He works hard = usilovně. He hardly works = sotva pracuje.

intro.title: You will use these words in
frames: It was a difficult … · *Bylo to těžké …*
intro.note: Every Quiz and Type item is an FCE cloze (B7): a full sentence with a gap and the root in CAPITALS. The chips are other forms of the **same** root, never another family's word.
intro.note_cz: Každá otázka je věta s mezerou a kořenem VELKÝMI písmeny.

items.gap: It was a difficult ____ because the two jobs were in different cities. (DECIDE)
The evening was a big ____, and everybody stayed late. (SUCCEED)
The police asked for a ____ of the man in the shop. (DESCRIBE)
We had no ____ but to wait for the next train. (CHOOSE)
Our ____ was late, so the shops were closed. (ARRIVE)
Her ____ was clear, but the students still asked three questions. (EXPLAIN)
The two companies signed an ____ in October. (AGREE)
The ____ of the new part of town will take ten years. (DEVELOP)
After a long ____ we chose the cheaper flat. (DISCUSS)
There is a big ____ in his English since September. (IMPROVE)
We need more ____ before we can book the tickets. (INFORM)
The teacher spoke to his parents about his ____. (BEHAVE)
The road is more ____ in winter than in summer. (DANGER)
She is the most ____ person in the company. (SUCCESS)
Be ____ with the glasses; they were my grandmother's. (CARE)
This book is more ____ than the one my teacher gave me. (USE)
A ____ breakfast costs less than people think. (HEALTH)
The lake is ____, not made by people. (NATURE)
The old chair is more ____ than the new one. (COMFORT)
The flat is cheap because the street is ____. (NOISE)
We were ____ with the weather all week. (LUCK)
The people in the village were very ____. (FRIEND)
The man at the desk was ____ and found us a room. (HELP)
The town is ____ for its beer. (FAME)
Please drive ____ because the road is wet after the rain. (CAREFUL)
He answered ____, but the answer was wrong. (QUICK)
He finished the work ____ because he had done it before. (EASY)
The children played ____ in the garden all afternoon. (HAPPY)
He is ____ looking for a new job. (ACTIVE)
Please speak more ____ on the phone. (CLEAR)
She spoke ____ about the problem, but nobody listened. (SERIOUS)
I cannot ____ finish this before Friday. (POSSIBLE)
She speaks English very ____ for a beginner. (GOOD)
He works ____, but he never talks about it. (HARD)
The old shop has ____ changed since last year. (COMPLETE)
I am ____ sorry about the mistake. (TRUE)

use_hint: Rewrite the sentence. Replace the underlined words.

use_sentences.prompt: It was a difficult thing to decide because the two jobs were in different cities.
use_sentences.en: It was a difficult decision because the two jobs were in different cities.
accepts: It was a difficult decision because the two jobs were in different cities

use_sentences.prompt: We had no other way but to wait for the next train.
use_sentences.en: We had no choice but to wait for the next train.
accepts: We had no choice but to wait for the next train

use_sentences.prompt: There is a big change for the better in his English since September.
use_sentences.en: There is a big improvement in his English since September.
accepts: There is a big improvement in his English since September
There's a big improvement in his English since September

use_sentences.prompt: The teacher spoke to his parents about his way of behaving.
use_sentences.en: The teacher spoke to his parents about his behaviour.
accepts: The teacher spoke to his parents about his behaviour

use_sentences.prompt: The road is more risky in winter than in summer.
use_sentences.en: The road is more dangerous in winter than in summer.
accepts: The road is more dangerous in winter than in summer

use_sentences.prompt: The old chair is more pleasant to sit in than the new one.
use_sentences.en: The old chair is more comfortable than the new one.
accepts: The old chair is more comfortable than the new one

use_sentences.prompt: The flat is cheap because the street is very loud.
use_sentences.en: The flat is cheap because the street is noisy.
accepts: The flat is cheap because the street is noisy

use_sentences.prompt: The man at the desk was very kind and found us a room.
use_sentences.en: The man at the desk was helpful and found us a room.
accepts: The man at the desk was helpful and found us a room

use_sentences.prompt: Please drive with care because the road is wet.
use_sentences.en: Please drive carefully because the road is wet.
accepts: Please drive carefully because the road is wet

use_sentences.prompt: Please speak in a clear way on the phone.
use_sentences.en: Please speak clearly on the phone.
accepts: Please speak clearly on the phone

use_sentences.prompt: The old shop has totally changed since last year.
use_sentences.en: The old shop has completely changed since last year.
accepts: The old shop has completely changed since last year

use_sentences.prompt: She is very good at her work in the company.
use_sentences.en: She is very successful in the company.
accepts: She is very successful in the company
